ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure, on the left side there is a CMOS structure controlled by inputs P and Q: the upper part is a pMOS pull-up branch connected to +VDD, and the lower part is an nMOS pull-down branch connected to ground; the common output of these devices is the middle horizontal node. On the right side of the figure there is also a pair of complementary pMOS/nMOS transistors, connected between +VDD and ground, whose gates are driven by this middle node, and the common terminal of the two is labeled OUT. Then reason: The left-side CMOS network controlled by P and Q is a NAND structure, because as long as P=0 or Q=0, there is a pull-up path; only when P=1 and Q=1 does the pull-down path conduct to ground. Therefore the middle node is NOT(P AND Q). The right-side complementary transistor pair forms an inverter, which inverts this NAND output again, so OUT = NOT(NOT(P AND Q)) = P AND Q.

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure: the P and Q controlled devices on the left form a CMOS NAND network whose output is the middle horizontal node, because the pull-up path exists when P=0 or Q=0 and the pull-down path to ground exists only when P=1 and Q=1. Then note from the image that this middle node drives the gates of the rightmost complementary pMOS/nMOS pair connected between +VDD and ground, with its joined output labeled OUT. Therefore the rightmost stage inverts the NAND result, giving OUT = NOT(NOT(P AND Q)) = P AND Q.
